name: commit-defender-gemini
description: AI-powered pre-commit code review with inline suggestions

commitDefender.pythonExecutable.description: Path to the python executable that has commit-defender installed. You can use ${workspaceFolder} as a prefix.

commitDefender.timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the Docker container.

commitDefender.runOnStage.description: Automatically analyze whenever files are staged (git add). Also available manually via the shield icon.

commitDefender.homeEnvFile.description: Absolute path to credentials .env file. Defaults to ~/.commit-defender.env.

enumDescriptions: hybrid: Run linters first, then send results + diff to AI for a combined review. (default)
ai-powered: Skip linters — send only the diff to the AI. Faster, no toolchain required.
rule-based: Run linters only — no AI call. Fully offline, deterministic.
commitDefender.analysisMode.description: Controls which analysis engines run. Leave empty to use the value in .commit-defender/settings.json (default: hybrid).

enumDescriptions: severe: Flag everything, zero tolerance for any deviation.
rigorous: Strict — flag most issues including minor style and best-practice deviations.
generous: Only flag significant issues, allow minor deviations.
lean: Only flag critical issues that would break functionality or introduce security risk.
commitDefender.severityLevel.description: Controls the strictness and harshness of the review. Lower levels produce fewer, higher-priority findings.

enumDescriptions: colorful: Elaborate feedback with examples, alternatives, and detailed explanations.
chatty: Detailed feedback with helpful context for each finding.
moderate: Standard amount of detail — clear but concise. (default)
simple: Brief, to-the-point findings with minimal explanation.
silent: One-line summaries only — no elaboration.
commitDefender.richnessLevel.description: Controls the quantity, detail level, and verbosity of the AI review output.

commitDefender.excludePatterns.description: Additional gitignore-style patterns to exclude from analysis (e.g. 'tests/**', '*.generated.ts'). These are merged with patterns in .commit-defender/settings.json.

enumDescriptions: azure-openai: Azure-hosted OpenAI models. Requires endpoint, api-version, and a deployment name as the model.
anthropic: Anthropic Claude models (claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-6, etc.).
openai: OpenAI platform (api.openai.com). Works with any model name like gpt-4o, o3, etc.
commitDefender.aiProvider.description: AI provider to use for code review.

commitDefender.model.description: Model or deployment name to use. Examples: 'claude-sonnet-4-6' (Anthropic), 'gpt-4o' (OpenAI), your deployment name (Azure). Leave empty to use the value in commit-defender.yaml.

commitDefender.endpoint.description: API endpoint URL. Required for azure-openai (e.g. https://YOUR_RESOURCE.openai.azure.com). For openai or anthropic, leave empty to use the default public endpoint.

commitDefender.apiVersion.description: API version string. Used by azure-openai only (e.g. 2024-08-01-preview). Ignored for anthropic and openai.

commitDefender.apiKey.description: API key for the selected provider. Store this in User Settings (not Workspace) to keep it out of source control. Alternatively, set AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY in ~/.commit-defender.env.

commitDefender.maxTokens.description: Maximum output tokens for the AI review response. Increase if you see 'Could not parse AI response as JSON' on large files (response was truncated mid-JSON).
